lanes.summary: The diff extends the existing CONTRACT_COUNT-only generator to all five previously hand-typed README counts (CRATE_COUNT, CLI_COMMAND_COUNT, BOOK_CLI_CHAPTER_COUNT, BOOK_LIB_CHAPTER_COUNT, CRATES_DIR_COUNT), matching G1 (--list-blocks, --write refuses missing block exit 3 / zero instrument exit 2, --check exact), G3 (readme_contract.rs now compares every *_COUNT block against `readme_sync.sh --print-all`, allowing lag but never overstatement), and G4 (batch_fold.sh generalizes its count-conflict regex to any *_COUNT block; session_docs_commit.sh delegates to readme_sync.sh --write instead of sed-patching). I independently re-measured three of the five new counts against the actual tree (book/src/cli = 114, book/src/lib = 73, contracts census n_files = 1837, and CLI registry commands section = 112 excluding help) and all matched the README's new claims exactly — no overstatement found. The old duplicate hand-typed crate-directory count in the ASCII tree diagram was removed rather than left as a second, ungenerated site, closing a drift vector the ticket's own commit message calls out. Supporting guard scripts (check_readme_claims.sh, check_readme_numeric_claims.sh, check_row_pr_write_set.sh, check_batch_fold.sh) were all updated to strip/handle the new generic markers, each with an added case-table row. The G2 PR-edit guard is explicitly out of scope here (assigned to a different branch/session per the roadmap note), consistent with ticket's 50%-progress status.

findings.claim: When README.md carries two occurrences of the SAME *_COUNT name with different values on the `ours` side of a merge (e.g. a pre-fold drift between the two CONTRACT_COUNT sites), `readme_counts_only`'s per-name sed pass applies globally (`/g`) per name, so the later-sorted value silently overwrites the earlier occurrence's value for all instances of that name rather than restoring each occurrence's own captured value.
findings.fix: Not blocking: the immediately following `--regen` step rewrites every block from the live measurement, so the transient merged value is self-healing; flagged for awareness only, no test in check_batch_fold.sh currently exercises multi-instance same-name divergence.

lanes.summary: GEN-001 widens the single-generator pattern from the CONTRACT_COUNT block to all five derived README counts (crate, contract, CLI command, book CLI/lib chapters, crate-directory). Verified: readme_sync.sh's BLOCKS/measure_*/--list-blocks/--print-all/--check/--write logic is self-consistent and matches the G1 exit-code contract (3 for missing block, 2 for zero/unmeasured); readme_contract.rs's new generator-driven test correctly strips markers and compares against --print-all; batch_fold.sh's generalized COUNT_RE with backreferences correctly extends the fold-as-generated behavior to all *_COUNT blocks; session_docs_commit.sh no longer sed-patches README itself, delegating to readme_sync.sh --write (G4); check_readme_claims.sh, check_readme_numeric_claims.sh and check_row_pr_write_set.sh were all updated to strip/detect markers so they don't go blind or vacuous. I independently verified against the live tree that the measured counts baked into README.md (CLI 112, book/cli 114, book/lib 73, crates/ dirs 86) match `ls book/src/cli/*.md` (114 files) and `ls book/src/lib/*.md` (73 files) exactly, and confirmed the contracts/readme-claims-v1.yaml key using "ls -Nd" (which looked like a typo for "-1d" at first glance) is in fact the correct normalized form produced by check_readme_numeric_claims.sh's own digit→N substitution regex. No other readme_contract.rs test reads raw unmarked README digits that this diff missed. No evidence the diff weakens a gate, contradicts its own tests, or does anything outside GEN-001's scope (the check_row_pr_write_set.sh touch is a necessary consequence of introducing markers, not scope creep).
